newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Telekom reports slow profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Telekom reports slow profit growth.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd on Friday reported a net profit of 889.9 million ringgit ($338.4 million) for the first half-year, well below market forecasts.

The telecommunications utility, the second largest capitalised stock on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, said a cut in international phone tariffs, slower installations and higher operating costs had affected half-year earnings.
But it predicted a better performance in the second half.
Telekom's net profit of 889.9 million ringgit for the six months to June 30 meant it managed only 5.7 percent earnings growth over the 841.8 million ringgit profit recorded in the first half of 1996.
Analysts had earlier this week forecast first-half growth of between 11 and 15 percent.
"The numbers are bad," said a telecommunications analyst at a foreign brokerage house.
Before tax, profit grew 9.1 percent to 1.20 billion ringgit.
Telekom said earnings per share were 35.6 cents against 42.2 cents in the first half of 1996, while group operating revenue rose 15.3 percent to 3.41 billion ringgit.

Explaining the slower growth, Telekom said in a statement accompanying the results: "First is the lower than expected revenue growth, attributable to slower line installation coupled with drop in call revenue due to tariff reduction."
"Secondly, there has been an increase in operating cost of 19.8 percent over the corresponding period in 1996..."
The jump in operating costs reflected higher labour costs, a provision for bad debt and increased interest costs.
Telekom said its ATUR 450 cellular-phone service saw a four percent drop in its customer base in the first six months to 83,000.
But its second and newer cellular-phone service, TMTouch, is poised for growth with its customer base expected to reach 100,000 by the end of the year, the company said.
Malaysia's cellular-phone service is very competitive with six other operators vying for market share.
"The telecommunications industry is still very competitive and the company is continuously positioning itself to sustain its performance in 1997," Telekom said.
But it was optimistic that the second half-year would be better.
"The board is confident that with continued improvement in productivity and quality of service, the performance of the group will be improved in the second half of the year."
At Friday's closing share price of 9.70 ringgit, the company is capitalised at 29.09 billion ringgit, second only to power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd at 32.24 billion ringgit.
